overview.historicalContext: The Jacobi-Trudi identity (1841, independently rediscovered by Trudi 1864) expresses Schur polynomials as determinants of complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials: s_λ = det[h_{λᵢ-i+j}]. This is foundational in algebraic combinatorics and representation theory: Schur polynomials are characters of GL(n) representations, and the Jacobi-Trudi formula connects them to the ring of symmetric functions. The LGV lemma provides the standard combinatorial proof via non-intersecting lattice paths and RSK correspondence.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the definition of Schur polynomials via the Jacobi-Trudi determinant formula and prove their key properties: symmetry, base cases, and the connection to the LGV lemma infrastructure already formalized in the parent gallery proofs.
overview.text: The key insight is that Mathlib's complete homogeneous symmetric polynomials hsymm σ R n provide exactly the building blocks for the Jacobi-Trudi matrix. The entry at position (i,j) is h_{sh_i + j - i} when i ≤ sh_i + j (else 0 to handle the h_n = 0 for n < 0 convention using ℕ subtraction). Symmetry of the Schur polynomial then follows from: (1) each matrix entry is symmetric (using hsymm_isSymmetric + rename_hsymm), and (2) AlgHom.map_det lets us push rename through the determinant.
overview.proofStrategy: For symmetry: AlgHom.map_det gives (rename e)(det M) = det((rename e).mapMatrix M), then show each entry (rename e)(h_{sh_i+j-i}) = h_{sh_i+j-i} using rename_hsymm. For base cases: det_fin_zero = 1, det_fin_one simplifies 1×1 determinant. For two-row: det_fin_two gives the 2×2 expansion. The LGV connection (SSYT ↔ NI paths via RSK) requires ~400 lines of additional formalization.
keyInsights: Mathlib's hsymm σ R n is precisely the h_n in the Jacobi-Trudi formula — no additional definitions needed
ℕ subtraction handles the h_n = 0 for n < 0 convention cleanly: check i ≤ sh_i + j before computing sh_i + j - i
AlgHom.map_det + rename_hsymm + split_ifs handles the symmetry proof in 10 lines
The LGV connection (RSK + SSYT) requires ~400 lines — left as open theorem placeholder
Schur polynomials are not in Mathlib 4 as of 2026; this file provides the first Lean 4 definition

sections.title: Part I: Definitions
sections.summary: Defines jacobiTrudiMatrix and schurPolynomial. Entry (i,j) = h_{sh_i+j-i} if i ≤ sh_i+j, else 0.
sections.mathContext: jacobiTrudiMatrix k sh : Matrix (Fin k) (Fin k) (MvPolynomial σ R). schurPolynomial k sh = det(jacobiTrudiMatrix). Uses ℕ subtraction with conditional to avoid negative indices.

sections.title: Part II: Base Cases
sections.summary: schurPolynomial_empty = 1 (0×0 det). schurPolynomial_one_row = hsymm σ R n (1×1 det).
sections.mathContext: det_fin_zero = 1 handles empty case. det_fin_one reduces to single entry. simp reduces the ℕ arithmetic.

sections.title: Part III: Symmetry
sections.summary: Each entry is symmetric (via hsymm_isSymmetric). Full symmetry via AlgHom.map_det.
sections.mathContext: IsSymmetric φ = ∀ e : Perm σ, rename e φ = φ. Key lemma: AlgHom.map_det gives (rename e)(det M) = det(mapMatrix (rename e) M). Then each entry: rename e (h_n) = h_n by rename_hsymm.

sections.title: Part IV: Two-Row Formula
sections.summary: Explicit formula for Schur([a,b]) = h_a*h_b - h_{a+1}*(h_{b-1} or 0).
sections.mathContext: det_fin_two gives the 2×2 expansion. Matrix.cons lemmas extract entries. The (1,0) entry check: if 1 ≤ b then h_{b-1} else 0.

sections.title: Part V: Hook-Length Connection
sections.summary: Evaluation at all-ones = C(n+k-1, k-1) = |Sym (Fin k) n|.
sections.mathContext: eval (fun _ => 1) (hsymm (Fin k) R n) = |Sym (Fin k) n| via map_sum and card_univ.
